newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu visits settlement in show of defiance.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu visits settlement in show of defiance.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu paid his first official visit to a Jewish settlement in the West Bank on Tuesday in a show of defiance to Palestinians opposed to his policy of expanding the outposts.

Netanyahu chose Ariel, one of the most entrenched Jewish communities in the West Bank, as the venue for his high-profile tour, a day after the Palestinian Authority called for an immediate halt of all settlement activity.

An Israeli military helicopter ferried him to Ariel, the second largest Jewish settlement in the West Bank occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East War. Ariel is home to some 13,000 Jews who live in apartment buildings and private houses.
Alighting from the helicopter, Netanyahu strode across a field towards the settlement's perimetre fence where hundreds of schoolchildren cheered the arrival of the right-wing leader.
He was due to deliver a speech at Ariel's community centre.
The visit was Netanyahu's first tour of a West Bank settlement since he took office in June after ousting Israel's previous centre-left government in May elections.
Netanyahu enraged Arabs by rescinding the former Labour-led government's freeze on new settlement building and nullifying Labour's policy of trading occupied Arab land for peace.

Settlement construction, seen by both sides as establishing "facts on the ground" beyond the bounds of talks, has been condemned as an obstacle to peace by Israel's ally Washington. But recent U.S. reaction to Netanyahu's moves has been muted.

Netanyahu has given the go-ahead for thousands of new homes in West Bank settlements, and hawkish ex-general Ariel Sharon, his minister for infrastructure, is overseeing planning for 900 housing units on the Israeli-occupied Syrian Golan Heights.

Under the 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal, Israel has handed over parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip to Palestinian self-rule but the fate of settlements has been left to "final-status" talks which have been frozen since Netanyahu's May election.

Palestinians have been killed in clashes with Israeli troops and settlers over confiscation of Arab land to build roads and settlements in the West Bank and Gaza where some 130,000 Jews live among the more than two million Palestinians.
